items.followUp: Compare bus topology and mesh topology with respect to layout, data transmission and reliability.

rubric.why: A star has a central connecting device, while a ring forms a closed loop.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the central-device layout of a star and the loop layout of a ring.

rubric.why: Star-network data passes through the central device; ring-network data travels around the ring.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing how data travels in both topologies.

rubric.why: The model answer contrasts disruption caused by failure of the star's central device with disruption from a break in the ring.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining relevant failure effects in both topologies.

rubric.why: A failure of an individual star connection can affect the device connected by that cable.
rubric.description: States the effect of a star connection failure
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting that a single star cable failure can affect its connected device.

modelAnswer: In a star topology, every computer is connected separately to a central hub or switch; in a ring topology, each computer is connected to its two neighbors to form a closed loop.
In a star, data passes through the central hub or switch; in a ring, data travels from device to device around the ring.
If the central hub or switch fails, communication in a star network is disrupted; failure of a single connection can affect the connected device.
A break in a ring can disrupt communication around the loop.

items.followUp: Define malware and write three signs that an email may be a scam.

rubric.why: Phishing is a deceptive attempt to obtain sensitive information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that phishing tricks people into revealing sensitive information.

rubric.why: Misleading senders, urgency, suspicious links and attachments can be characteristics of phishing emails.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid email characteristic.

rubric.why: A phishing website may imitate a genuine site or use a misleading address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing an imitation site or misleading web address.

rubric.why: Phishing messages or websites may ask users for sensitive details.
rubric.description: Identifies information requested by phishing messages or websites
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a type of sensitive information that may be requested.

modelAnswer: A phishing attack is a fraudulent attempt to trick people into revealing sensitive information by pretending to be a trustworthy person or organization.
A phishing email may come from a misleading sender, use urgent language, or contain a suspicious link or attachment.
A phishing website imitates a genuine website and may use a misleading web address.
It may ask visitors to enter passwords, bank details or other personal information.

items.followUp: Write down any two disadvantages of an algorithm.

rubric.why: An algorithm presents a solution in clear, ordered steps, making it easier to understand.
rubric.description: States one valid advantage of an algorithm
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid advantage, such as clarity or ease of understanding.

rubric.why: An algorithm can be translated into programs written in different programming languages.
rubric.description: States another valid advantage of an algorithm
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct valid advantage.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is easy to understand because it presents a solution in clear, step-by-step form.
An algorithm is language-independent and can be translated into a program in different programming languages.
